name: Perlin mapped to Gaussian by erfinv
plain: Makes one octave of Perlin noise per channel, then multiplies its absolute value by a million and takes it modulo 11, scaled to [0,1). That scrambles the field to roughly uniform values, which go through the inverse normal CDF. The result is roughly Gaussian in value and has little Perlin structure left. A min-max helper exists but is not called.

props.normalizes_variance: approximate; not exact because Perlin values are not uniform in [0,1]

providers.author: NeuralSamurAI
providers.note: Source header cites Extraltodeus noise_latent_perlinpinpin; that repo is not in the library

label: from code
surprise: Min-max gives exactly 0 and 1 at extremes, erfinv gives ±inf there, and the clamp hides it at ±5.

audit.note: No min-max scaling happens: scale_tensor (dimensional_latent_perlin.py:66) is never called. Line 63 does remainder(|P|·10⁶,11)/11, which scrambles the field into near-uniform values, so little Perlin structure should survive. Line 87 calls one octave at res (1,1), persistence 1. Structure claim is by reading, not run.
